hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3, an arm on the candidate (s3c-ann-net), in two forms. Development tier

why: #1320 found that immediate-release cash management bill (CMB) days carry 67% of (s3c-ann-net)'s 2020 loss against (s3c), and that (s3c-ann) loses on bill settlement days with a CMB (352 development days; grid CRPS -3.0% at h = 2, upper-tail twCRPS losses at h = 2 to 4). In (s3c-ann-net) a CMB settlement is one of the bill auctions summed into the signed net bill, so a CMB shifts the spread by the same fitted amount per USD 100 bn as a regular bill. A CMB is ad hoc, is on no published schedule and is financing the Treasury asks for at short notice; the arm gives it its own coefficient, which the fit can set apart from the regular bill leg.

An announcement stamped 12:00 on its announcemt_date is public from 12:00, so any decision instant from 12:00 to 23:59 counts the same auctions.

candidates.name: sc_s3c_ann_net_cmbf
candidates.label: (s3c-ann-net-cmb), flag form
candidates.definition: (s3c-ann-net) with the CMB leg split out of the bill leg. Three settlement terms: the signed announced net coupon (unchanged, USD 100 bn); the signed announced net bill WITHOUT the CMB offerings (net bill ex-CMB, USD 100 bn: the (s3c-ann-net) net bill less the offerings of the CMBs counted in it, so that net bill ex-CMB + the CMB offering equals (s3c-ann-net)'s net bill wherever the bill class is counted; the class's maturing amount stays with the regular bills); and `cmb_flag`, 1 when the offering amounts of the CMBs settling on the target day T that had been announced by the decision instant of D = T - h sum to more than zero, else 0. The two nets enter as (s3c-ann-net)'s sized terms (scarcity state held at its maximum, so the regressor is the signed size over USD 100 bn); `cmb_flag` enters as an extra term after them. The CMB term enters the fit of a lead when at least three training pairs carry it (the rule of every flag of the fit, MIN_FLAGGED); the nets enter as in (s3c-ann-net). Everything else is (s3)'s: the other terms, the Huber fit (k = 1.345), the ridge of 5, the pool of standardised residuals and the direct pairs; the SRF cap at the line from full allotment, margin 0 bp, is applied to the quantiles exactly as to (s3)'s (repo_model.s3c_candidate, unchanged).
candidates.module: repo_model.s3c_announced (CMB_FLAG_ARM = ANN_NET_ARM with extra = (cmb_flag,); AnnouncedNetExCmbSizeTable for the two nets; AnnouncedCmbTerms for the CMB term); the fit is repo_model.spread_mr_state_calendar's with the CMB names added to its extra terms; no behaviour of an existing arm changes
candidates.units: cmb_flag: 0/1, effect in bp per flagged day; net_coupon and net bill ex-CMB: USD 100 bn, effect in bp per USD 100 bn

candidates.name: sc_s3c_ann_net_cmbs
candidates.label: (s3c-ann-net-cmb), size form
candidates.definition: As the flag form, with `cmb_size` in place of `cmb_flag`: the sum of the offering amounts of the CMBs settling on T that had been announced by the decision instant of D = T - h, in units of USD 100 bn (zero where none is announced). The CMB leg's net is its announced offering: a CMB's maturing amount is part of the bill class's maturing figure on the day it matures (one total for every bill of the class, net_settlement.net_for_day), which stays with the net bill ex-CMB, so the offering is the new money the CMB settlement adds. Net coupon and net bill ex-CMB are as in the flag form.
candidates.module: repo_model.s3c_announced (CMB_SIZE_ARM = ANN_NET_ARM with extra = (cmb_size,); the same two tables)
candidates.units: cmb_size: USD 100 bn (a USD 60 bn CMB reads 0.60), effect in bp per USD 100 bn; the nets as above

justification_of_two_forms: Both forms are declared because the data do not decide between them before a score: the flag asks whether a CMB settles at all (the reading (s3c-ann) uses for the bill leg), the size asks whether the shift grows with the amount (the reading (s3c-ann-net) uses). #1320's H-a for the bill leg was undecided, so neither form is preferred in advance. Neither is tuned; each is scored once.

new_read.what: the announced CMB term (`cmb_flag`, `cmb_size`) and the announced net bill without the CMB offerings
new_read.availability: a CMB auction's offering amount, settlement date and `cash_management_bill_cmb` flag are public from 12:00 America/New_York on its announcemt_date (metadata/settlement_announcement_dating.json, #541, measured and off; the same Fiscal Data records repo_model.net_settlement reads; the field `cash_management_bill_cmb` is already read by src/repo_model/net_settlement.py and nothing new is fetched). The figure for target day T at lead h counts a CMB only when its announcement is at or before the decision instant of the panel day h rows before T. A training pair reads the figure of its own decision (T - h), so a training figure and a forecast figure are the same function of the same announcements.
new_read.finding_1301: A CMB announced and settled inside the lead window, that is announced after the decision instant of T - h, is not readable at that lead and is not counted (the CMB is 0 there). Of the 458 CMBs settling inside the panel, 403 were announced five Monday-to-Friday days before settlement (metadata/announcement_release_times_1301.json), so most are readable at lead 5 and every shorter lead; the rest are readable only from the lead at which their announcement precedes the decision. At lead 1 the panel carries no CMB column, so the CMB term is read from the announcement at lead 1 as at every other lead, by the same function.
new_read.leakage_boundary: repo_model.s3c_announced.AnnouncedCmbTerms.read re-derives the CMB figure from the announced CMB auctions at the decision instant and compares it with the figure the table serves: a figure that counts a CMB announced after that instant raises LookAheadError, one that leaves an announced CMB out raises StaleReadError; the net bill ex-CMB is re-checked against the net announced at the instant by AnnouncedNetExCmbSizeTable.read (LookAheadError). tests/test_s3c_announced_cmb_1356.py holds the leakage test with one recorded mutation.
new_read.caveat: Lens E's caveat (docs/reviews/2026-10-19-five-lens/lens-E-data-plumbing.md, item G) applies in full: Treasury publishes no clock time for an announcement of a CMB; 153 of the 163 announcements that say 'for immediate release' are CMBs, and the 12:00 instant of those is unverified. If one is released after the 18:00 decision of its announcement day, the term counts it a decision too early. The page reports how many scored CMB settlement days rest on an immediate-release announcement and scores those days on their own.
new_read.bill_class_gate: (s3c-ann-net)'s net_for_day leaves a bill class that is partly announced at 0.0 (#679). The CMB term is not gated by it: a CMB announced by the instant is public whatever else is scheduled that day. Where the class is left out the net bill ex-CMB is 0.0 as (s3c-ann-net)'s net bill is, and the CMB term is the announced CMB offering. The page counts the scored days on which the two readings differ for this reason.
new_read.not_read_elsewhere: no published declaration, record or live path reads it

primary.metric: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5
primary.pressure_probability: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp), the probability read off the 23 quantiles as 1 - F(floor(tau) + 0.5), F linear between them (spread_mean_reversion.exceedance), the event strict and on whole basis points (data.exceeds_bp)
primary.calibration: the coverage of the central 90% band (q5 to q95, closed) of every model, pooled and by regime; a rate, reported as a mean and not tested
primary.comparisons: each form against (s3c-ann-net), (s3c), B1, B1' and B2, paired. On the settlement-day-type splits each form is tested against (s3c-ann-net) and (s3c) only, for length

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1356, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009): a form is read better than a reference when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page
scoring.splits: pooled; by lead; by regime (the declared regimes, 2018-19 and 2020 on their own among them); 2020 split into March to June (target months 3 to 6) and the rest of 2020, as #1320 did; by pressure-day type of the target day (turn_days.reporting_day_type, the record in force); by the settlement-day type of the target at each lead h = 1..5 (a coupon settlement day, a bill settlement day, a bill settlement day with a cash management bill, a bill settlement day without one, a day with neither: the panel's gross settlement above zero on the target day, and net_settlement.Auction.cmb for the CMB). 'Cash management bill settlement days against other bill days' is the pair (a bill settlement day with a cash management bill) against (a bill settlement day without one). The 2026 development days are the second window and carry the same splits. The intervals of a group of target days keep the current method (the group's days, scattered, resampled in date order as if consecutive), which #1221 questions and #1228 will decide
scoring.immediate_release: the scored target days on which a CMB with no stated release time (metadata/announcement_release_times_1301.json, 'immediate') settles, scored against the other CMB settlement days at each lead where the group has 20 days or more, and 2020 with those days left out, as #1320's table 4d did
scoring.identical_groups: a group in which an arm's score equals the reference's on every day is listed as identical and not tested against it; a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested

fitted_effect.what: the fitted effect of each settlement term in bp (per flagged day, or per USD 100 bn), by lead and regime of the target day: the mean over the scored decision days of the refit the forecast used times the anchor's scale, with the share of days on which the term was in the fit; for (s3c-ann-net) its net bill beside, so that the CMB coefficient can be read against the regular bill coefficient
fitted_effect.interval: the 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval over decision days (block 10, 2000 replications, seed 1356) of each mean; an interval over days that share refits, not a sampling interval for a coefficient

answer_asked: Whether the arm removes the 2020 loss of (s3c-ann-net) against (s3c) (the 2020 regime and March to June 2020 inside it), and at what cost elsewhere (the other regimes, the leads, the pressure-day types, the bill settlement days without a CMB, the 2026 days). Said plainly on the page, from the intervals, with no verdict.
reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c-ann-net) stays the candidate of avenue #1318 and (s3c) the H5 candidate until she rules.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the lead, regime and settlement-day-type splits beside it.

If a form should replace (s3c-ann-net), that goes to her as a marked question with numbered options and a default that changes no claim; the candidate does not change in this directive. Adopting the arm is her decision.
The CMB term is read with Lens E's caveat on the announcement time of a cash management bill.
